subject: Post-demo candidate slate, tradeoffs, and prompt inventory
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo candidate slate, tradeoffs, and prompt inventory

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + the three recommended candidate engines with concise tradeoffs and next steps so we all have the same page. I also attached the benchmark summary and the prompt pack we ran in the call (links below).

TL;DR — recommended slate (ordered by our suggested pilot path):
- rw-7b-q4f16 (Quantized Redwood 7B) — Lowest cost per token, median latency in our hosting ~110ms/token for 512-context, very strong on concise summarization and instruction following. Slightly weaker on rare factual retrieval and long-context consistency.
- open-13b-gguf (13B GGUF optimized) — Middle cost, better factuality / recall on longer prompts, median latency ~180ms/token on the same runner. Good fall-back when rw-7b produces hallucinations.
- 30b-sparse (30B sparse variant) — Highest quality, best at long-form coherence and multi-turn context, but material cost increase (~3-4x) and higher latency; use only for final-inference post-filtering or occasional high-value flows.

Why this slate? Brightline's priority is: 1) keep customer-facing latencies under 250ms for short replies; 2) limit per-conversation cost to hit the economics you outlined; 3) maintain high quality on guided summarization and entity extraction. The three candidates give a clear cost/latency/quality frontier and a straightforward fallback path.

Benchmarks & prompt inventory attached / linked:
- Benchmark summary (PDF): benchmarks_brightline_q2.pdf — includes cost per 1k tokens, latency percentiles, and accuracy on your sample prompts.
- Prompt pack (TXT): prompt_pack_brightline_v1.txt — canonical prompts used during evaluation plus a small regression suite.
- Live links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_benchmarks and https://docs.redwood.com/prompt-packs/brightline-v1

Operational notes / guardrails we recommend for pilot:
- Canary rollout: start with rw-7b for 80% traffic, open-13b for 15% (fallback for hallucination detection), 30b-sparse held for <5% high-value sessions.
- Prefix caching: enable KV prefix caching for user session tokens to shave ~20-30ms on repeated interactions.
- Token limits & truncation: set hard token cap at 1024 for user input and 2048 for context in the pilot to keep latency bounded.
- Regression detection: run the prompt_pack against both rw-7b and open-13b nightly during the pilot. We’ll flag any drop >5% in correctness on entity extraction.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm pilot slate and acceptance criteria (quality thresholds + latency SLO).
2) Redwood to provision a 2-week pilot pool (reserved burst + hosted) and provide detailed cost projection for 100k monthly active users.
3) Sign the attached SOW draft to lock pilot dates; procurement can be looped in (cc’d).

Action items for Brightline: please confirm preferred pilot start window (earliest we can start is 2027-06-07) and any additional evaluation metrics you want added.

Attachments: benchmarks_brightline_q2.pdf (7 pages), prompt_pack_brightline_v1.txt (21 prompts), SOW-draft-Brightline.docx (stub)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to walk through the metric thresholds.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184
https://redwood.com
From: Elena Morozova <elena@brightline.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo candidate slate, tradeoffs, and prompt inventory

Jonas — this is helpful, thanks. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 
1) For the nightly regression run, can you include a precision/recall breakdown for entity extraction rather than a single correctness metric? We need to understand false positives vs false negatives.
2) The latency numbers you quoted — are those median p50 on the hosted Redwood cluster in us-west-2 with 4x A10s? We expect slightly worse performance if we run on our GCP region.
3) For the canary split, what observability hooks will we get in the console? We want token-level costs and a way to set automated fallback when open-13b confidence drops.

Procurement — we’ll need a one-page pilot SOW and an invoice process; cc’ing procurement@brightline.ai (explicit permission to loop them).

Assuming answers are reasonable, we’re ready to proceed to the pilot. Proposed start week: 2027-06-14 (one week later than your earliest).

—
Elena Morozova
Head of Product, Brightline AI
elena@brightline.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Elena Morozova <elena@brightline.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo candidate slate, tradeoffs, and prompt inventory

Jonas — two quick procurement notes while we draft the one-page SOW: 
- Pricing baseline: for pilot budgeting assume rw-7b at $0.003/token equivalent (hosted), open-13b at $0.009/token, and 30b-sparse at $0.025/token. I’ll attach a simple cost spreadsheet in the hub. These are pilot estimates and will vary with token mix.
- Invoice cadence: Brightline usually needs a PO before spend; can we accept a PO and bill monthly? If so, we’ll mark the pilot as month-to-month with conversion to a committed Dedicated contract if you hit >3M tokens/month.

Also — Jonas, can you enable the nightly regression run to output precision/recall per entity label (Elena Q1)? We can wire that into the Redwood console alerts.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo candidate slate, tradeoffs, and prompt inventory

Great — thanks Elena and Ben. Quick confirmations and next-steps: 
- Precision/recall: confirmed. We’ll add per-entity precision/recall to the nightly regression report and surface delta alerts >5% on any label.
- Latency baseline: numbers quoted are for our managed us-west-2 cluster with 4x A10s. If you run in your GCP eu-west region we should expect ~10–20% higher median latency; we’ll include a region-adjusted projection in the cost sheet.
- Observability: Redwood console will provide token-level cost, p50/p95 latency per route, per-model rollup, and a webhook that can trigger automatic fallback to open-13b when confidence <0.6 (or custom threshold).

Procurement path: Ben will follow up with the one-page SOW and the pilot cost spreadsheet. Elena — accepting 2027-06-14 as pilot start is fine; we’ll target provisioning week-of 2027-06-07 for final config and smoke tests.

I’ve uploaded the SOW-draft and benchmark PDF to the Drive link above; Ben will send the HubSpot deal id for procurement reference (BR-2027-117).

If all good, I’ll schedule a 20-min sync for next Tue (2027-05-25) to finalize the SLOs and sign-off items.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
